name: Joseph F. Smith
role: Sixth President of the Church; received section 138
dateNote: He reported the vision in section 138 on 3 October 1918, about six weeks before his death on 19 November 1918.
importance: Section 138 is his account of a vision of the spirit world, received while he pondered Christ’s visit to the dead. The vision says the Savior organized faithful spirits to preach to those in prison. It names many he saw there, including his father Hyrum Smith. The text was later added to the scriptures.
connections: He was the son of Hyrum Smith and Mary Fielding Smith and a nephew of Joseph Smith. He served as Church president from 1901 to 1918.

sources.title: Joseph F. Smith, Church History Topics

reviewNote: Wikipedia: born 13 Nov. 1838, Far West; died 19 Nov. 1918, Salt Lake City; president from 1901; vision 3 Oct. 1918, canonized 1976 (Pearl of Great Price, later D&C 138). Church History Topics confirms parents, 1866 apostleship, 1901 presidency, 1918 vision. JSP has no usable page. The section text names him only as “I” and “my father, Hyrum Smith”, so no linkNames.
